args.body: Based on FY26Q1 data across 8 segments, the exposure-weighted portfolio loss ratio is 0.712241. The pricing model recommends a rate of 0.030567 (base rate: 0.0412, loading: -25.81%) to achieve a target combined ratio of 0.96.

The portfolio loss ratio was computed as an exposure-weighted mean of all 8 segment loss ratios using FY26Q1 data. Segment loss ratios ranged from 0.589 (property_sme_east) to 0.827 (liability_professional). The pricing model was run against this portfolio loss ratio with a target combined ratio of 0.96 to derive the recommended rate.

Key risks include: (1) liability_professional segment has the highest loss ratio (0.827) and severity (244500 INR), (2) property_sme_east shows high burn cost (6.78) due to high severity relative to exposure units, (3) marine_cargo_west also exhibits elevated burn cost (5.12), and (4) reinsurance cede percentages vary significantly from 8% to 45%, affecting net loss positions. The negative loading of -25.81% suggests the current portfolio may be overpriced relative to target combined ratio.

Based on FY26Q1 data across 8 segments, the exposure-weighted portfolio loss ratio is 0.712241. The pricing model recommends a rate of 0.030567 (base rate 0.0412, loading -25.81%) to achieve a target combined ratio of 0.96.

The portfolio loss ratio was computed as an exposure-weighted mean of segment-level loss ratios using FY26Q1 data. The pricing model was run with this portfolio loss ratio and a target combined ratio of 0.96 to derive the recommended rate.

Key risks include potential adverse loss development in high-severity segments (property_sme_east, liability_professional), reinsurance dependency variability, and exposure concentration in health_group_corporate. The negative loading reflects favorable portfolio performance but may not persist if loss trends reverse.
